extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical and chemistry faculty; institutional officials and research administrators at participating U.S. research universities/institutes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility/selection criteria for nomination and application to the Searle Scholars Program, which funds independent, early-career biomedical and chemistry investigators. Covers nomination rules, eligibility exceptions, award amounts, timeline, and selection priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be nominated by a participating institution in order to apply for our program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may only apply if they have been nominated by an invited institution; consult the institutional official designated for your institution on the program's list for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating/invited institutions only
rubrics_metrics.description: Only participating institutions are eligible to field applicants to the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program partners with leading research institutions and universities to nominate promising research faculty; see the Process and Eligibility page for how institutions get invited to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible candidate profile — early-career faculty in biomedical sciences and chemistry
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program makes grants to support the independent research of exceptional young faculty in the biomedical sciences and chemistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating institutions may nominate outstanding early-career scientists to apply; program aims to 'jumpstart' early careers and invest in promising young scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection priorities — creative, innovative, high risk/high reward research
rubrics_metrics.description: A Scientific Advisory Board evaluates applications aimed at finding creative, innovative, and 'high risk/high reward' research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Advisory Board consists of prestigious researchers (many former Searle Scholars) who help guide the program and evaluate applications for each class of Scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and term
rubrics_metrics.description: Searle Scholars Award Grants are set at $450,000 for a three-year period with $150,000 payable each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are made to participating institutions (see payment and institutional eligibility); view Award Info for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award recipient entity and tax status
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are made to tax-exempt institutions described in section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code; awards are not made to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must be legally employed at a qualifying U.S. degree-granting or research institution which will receive the grant on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment requirement (institutional location)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must be legally employed at a United States degree granting or research institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though applicants need not be U.S. citizens, employment at a U.S. institution is required for award eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship — not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are not required to be U.S. citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, awardees must be legally employed at a U.S. degree-granting or research institution, and awards are made to U.S. tax-exempt institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MD-only investigators eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Basic biological scientists who hold only an M.D. degree are eligible as long as they are researchers and not purely clinicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, their research must contain basic science components — clinical-only practice without basic-science research focus is not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on other funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program does not place any restrictions on funding from other sources of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Searle Scholars award is meant to supplement other funding received by an investigator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited submission process / invitation status
rubrics_metrics.description: The Searle Scholars Program is a limited submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an institution is not on the participating/invited list, its faculty cannot apply. Institutions must be invited/participating to nominate applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timeline and submission method
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are accepted annually from June through September, only through an online application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should follow the online system and consult the Award Timeline for deadlines and milestone dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of extenuating circumstances for eligibility dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The Program considers extenuating circumstances and may make exceptions on a case by case basis for applicants whose start date is slightly before the stated eligibility date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favorable considerations include a start date very close to the stated date, an unusually short period of postdoctoral training, and parental leave; contact the Scientific Director for exception requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: How institutions obtain participation/invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions may be invited to participate in the program; see Process and Eligibility for details on how an institution gets invited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions designated as participating are responsible for nominating candidates and naming an institutional official for coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose — supporting independent, bold early-career research
rubrics_metrics.description: The program funds independent research to allow early-career scientists to conceive and initiate bold new research directions alongside more conventional studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program narratives and scholar testimonials emphasize intellectual freedom and long-term lab development as outcomes of Searle support.
